ceiling_statement: Maximum achievable plan-decomposition assurance under H1-H8 is: for a plan committed as a finite, explicitly typed dataflow DAG with a declared goal-artifact set, ALL defects in the decidable defect class — cyclic dependency, produces/consumes artifact-type mismatch on any edge, goal artifact unreachable from admitted inputs, orphan stage feeding no goal, ambiguous execution order — are made structurally inadmissible at plan-definition time (fail-closed macroexpansion, H3), the admitted plan has a unique deterministic total schedule (H5), and the plan carries a certificate that any third party re-derives from the committed plan bytes alone (H8). No feasible system can additionally verify completeness of the plan relative to informal human intent, nor decide plan existence over unbounded action spaces.
derivation: (1) Verification theory: 'is this decomposition complete?' relative to intent is not computable — the intent is not encoded in the machine; the only machine-checkable question is completeness relative to a committed formal goal specification. This is model-independent underdetermination, identical in kind to AX-01's text/meaning gap. (2) Complexity: general plan synthesis (STRIPS-style) is PSPACE-complete and undecidable over infinite domains — but H5+H6 force the plan to exist as a committed finite artifact BEFORE execution (deterministic replay requires a frozen plan; all-or-nothing transitions require knowing the transition set). Against a committed finite DAG with finitely many typed edges, every property in the defect class above is decidable in O(V+E) and its certificate is checkable in linear time; therefore FULL exclusion of the decidable class, not statistical reduction of it, is feasible — and per the CLAUDE.md supreme law, elimination of the error class is the ceiling, guarding against instances is below it. (3) Determinism: among valid schedules, uniqueness is achievable at zero cost (topological sort with total lexicographic tie-break), and any nondeterministic schedule strictly violates H5, so the ceiling includes schedule uniqueness. Exceeding this ceiling would require either deciding intent (not encoded, information-theoretically impossible) or verifying unbounded plan spaces (undecidable).
relativity_note: Relative to the committed typed-DAG plan semantics: a finite set of stages with declared :produces/:consumes artifact types and a declared goal-artifact set (the DEFPIPELINE formalism of systems/orchestrator-spec/pipeline-dsl.lisp). 'Plan completeness' is completeness w.r.t. that committed goal set — never w.r.t. unformalized intent.
attainment_mechanism: B0 already holds every ingredient: the DEFPIPELINE DSL and stage classes with :produces metadata (systems/orchestrator-spec/pipeline-dsl.lisp, verified present), deterministic topological sort (systems/orchestrator-core/dependency-graph.lisp), a real staged DAG instance (systems/orchestrator-gr-syntagma/pipeline.lisp), the 5-stage cognition decomposition (source/cognition.lisp), and the single public write seat (systems/orchestrator-omega-modules/unified-frbr-generator.lisp). The ceiling mechanism: move the already-computed produces/consumes match INTO the DEFPIPELINE macroexpansion as a fail-closed compile-time error (any cycle, type mismatch, unreachable goal, orphan stage, or tie-break ambiguity aborts macroexpansion — the defective plan cannot come into existence, satisfying 'structurally impossible, not forbidden'); fix intra-tier order by lexicographic stage-name tie-break in dependency-graph.lisp; emit a plan certificate (S-expression of nodes, typed edges, goal set, schedule, plus SHA-256 over the canonical plan serialization via source/hash-authority.lisp) that an independent checker recomputes from the plan bytes. Plain SBCL macros + existing graph code + SHA-256 — constructible today with no new dependencies.
b0_gap: B0 map AX-02 row: the stage :produces-to-consumer artifact-type match is 'computed but NOT gated' — the single named weakness — so a type-mismatched plan is currently admissible; there is no machine-proof of one-entry composition and no plan certificate artifact. Adjacent AX-03/AX-14 residuals bear directly on the schedule half of this ceiling: systems/orchestrator-core/parallel-executor.lisp swallows per-stage errors to nil, marks failed stages executed, and runs intra-tier in nondeterministic order — all three violate the fail-closed unique-schedule ceiling and must be closed at their seat.
lean_obligation: Model a plan as P = (S : Finset Stage, produces : Stage -> Finset Typ, consumes : Stage -> Finset Typ, goals : Finset Typ, inputs : Finset Typ) with edge relation E s t := (produces s ∩ consumes t).Nonempty. Prove: (T1) gate soundness+completeness — the admission predicate `wf P` holds iff (acyclic E) ∧ (every consumed type on every edge is produced by exactly the declared producer type) ∧ (every g ∈ goals is reachable from inputs via E) ∧ (every stage lies on some inputs-to-goals path); (T2) schedule uniqueness — for wf P, the tie-broken topological sort is the UNIQUE function sched : P -> List Stage satisfying the linearization spec (determinism as a theorem, not a test); (T3) certificate faithfulness — cert(P) verifies iff wf P (the checker accepts no non-well-formed plan and rejects no well-formed one); (T4) completeness relative to goals — wf P implies every goal artifact possesses a finite derivation path from admitted inputs. All statements are over Finset/List with decidable predicates — directly Lean 4 formalizable.
